stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: A magnetic field $\vec{B}$ points OUT of the page. Drag the emitter to aim the velocity $\vec{v}$, use the $v_0$ slider to set the speed, then FIRE the positive charge. Watch how the Lorentz force $\vec{F} = q\,\vec{v} \wedge \vec{B}$ (drawn in orange on the particle) stays perpendicular to $\vec{v}$ and curves the path into a circle.
stages.concept: Lorentz force: $\vec{F} = q\,\vec{v} \wedge \vec{B}$. With $\vec{B} \perp \vec{v}$, $|\vec{F}| = q\,v\,B$ and $\vec{F}$ always points toward the centre of the circle. The particle moves in a circle of radius $r = \dfrac{m\,v}{q\,B}$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Hit all three targets inside the field. The dashed preview circle shows where the trajectory will go — aim, tune $v_0$, then FIRE. Remember: with $q > 0$ and $\vec{B}$ out of the page, the particle curves to the RIGHT of $\vec{v}$.
stages.concept: Radius depends only on the speed: $r = \dfrac{m\,v}{q\,B}$. The centre of the circle sits at $90^{\circ}$ to the right of $\vec{v}$ (right-hand rule for $+q$). Doubling $v_0$ doubles $r$; the period $T = \dfrac{2\pi m}{q B}$ stays the same.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: No preview circle. Read each target's coordinates $(x, z)$, apply the right-hand rule to find the centre direction, and pick $\alpha$ and $v_0$ so the arc sweeps through the target. You have one shot per target — no spray-and-pray.
stages.concept: The centre $C$ of the arc lies at distance $r = \dfrac{m v}{q B}$ perpendicular-right of $\vec{v}$. A target at $(x_T, z_T)$ is reachable iff it lies on that circle: $|CT| = r$. Combined with the centre direction, this fixes $\alpha$ and $v_0$.

labels.tip1: aim v, change v₀, then FIRE
labels.tip2: use the preview circle to line up each target
labels.tip3: compute α and v₀ from the target coordinates, then FIRE
labels.peek_tip_radius: Radius scales with speed: r = m·v / (q·B). Doubling v₀ doubles the arc radius; the period T = 2πm/(qB) is unchanged.
labels.peek_tip_centre: The centre of the arc sits 90° to the RIGHT of v (right-hand rule for q > 0, B out of page). Draw that perpendicular first — the target must lie r away from it.
labels.peek_tip_geometry: Two unknowns (α, v₀), two constraints: target on the circle AND centre perpendicular-right of v at distance r. Solve r from the target-emitter geometry first.

1.1: Drag the emitter head to change the launch direction α of v.
1.2: The v₀ slider on the right sets the launch speed. Larger v₀ = larger circle.
1.3: The orange arrow F on the particle is the Lorentz force. Notice it always points from the particle toward the centre of the circle.

2.1: The dashed circle previews the full trajectory. Move it around by adjusting α and v₀.
2.2: Speed sets the radius (r ∝ v₀). Angle rotates the circle around the emitter — the centre of the circle is always perpendicular-right of v.
2.3: If a target is inside the reachable ring, two (α, v₀) pairs usually hit it — try a small radius vs a large one to see.

3.1: Read each target's (x, z). Sketch the emitter, the target, and the perpendicular-right direction of v on paper.
3.2: For a given α, the centre C = (r sin α, −r cos α) from the emitter. The target must satisfy (x − r sin α)² + (z + r cos α)² = r².
3.3: Expand: x² + z² = 2r(x sin α − z cos α). Given a chosen α, this gives r = (x² + z²) / [2 (x sin α − z cos α)], then v₀ = r · (q B / m).
